name: a-frost-park-from-above
idea: Beat A, 1919. A high, wide view down onto a frosted city park on a winter morning, the bench small in the lower third with bare trees, iron railings and a lamp post around it, and the upper third left as empty pale sky for the caption. Dense, careful crosshatching in the manner of the precise newspaper draughtsmen of the period, perfect perspective, every railing and branch inked. The fat top-hatted man sits upright taking up most of the bench, one gloved palm raised flat in dismissal; the veteran, in a greatcoat with one trouser leg pinned up and a crutch across his knees, leans toward him. Their breath shows as small inked puffs in the cold.

name: a-crayon-dismissing-hand
idea: Beat A, 1919, drawn not with a pen but in black grease crayon and grey ink wash on rough board, soft smudged blacks and grainy tone. Close and low: the rich man's fat gloved hand flicking away fills the foreground in sharp focus, his jowly profile and top hat just behind it; the wounded soldier's face sits soft and out of focus further back, eyes on the hand. Late dusk, a single gas lamp off frame casting long tone across the board. Caption space falls in the dark empty upper area.

name: a-behind-the-bench-noon
idea: Beat A, 1919, seen from directly behind the bench: two backs, one vast in a frock coat and top hat, one thin in khaki with a crutch propped against the slats and a single boot below. Loose, quick, confident pen line with little hatching, printed on yellowed newsprint, the noon sun overhead pooling short shadows under the seat. The rich man's head is turned slightly away, one arm thrown out sideways in a lazy wave-off; the soldier's head is bowed. Beyond them a sunny promenade with strollers in boaters, drawn lightly so the pair dominate; caption room in the pale path at the bottom.

name: b-flat-colour-hospital-night
idea: Beat B, today. Flat colour in the old Munich satirical-magazine manner: heavy confident black outlines, three or four flat inks only (black, sodium orange, hospital teal, paper cream), no gradients. Night, the same style of park bench now outside a modern hospital's lit entrance, a sodium lamp above. The unchanged top-hatted rich man in his 1910s frock coat sits sprawled, palm out to the side; beside him a nurse in teal scrubs and trainers, hair escaping a clip, holds a paper cup of vending coffee and stares ahead. A black empty sky band at the top holds the caption.

name: b-two-eras-two-pens
idea: Beat B, today, medium two-shot at eye level on a grey rainy afternoon. The trick is in the drawing: the rich man is rendered in thick antique 1910s crosshatching, sepia-black, like a cut-out from an old newspaper, while the nurse and the modern street behind her (bus stop, wet pavement, phone in her hand) are drawn in clean, thin modern ink line with soft grey wash. He waves her off without looking at her; she has her lanyard and a hospital-issue rain jacket over scrubs. Rain streaks in fine ink; the top quarter is a pale grey sky for the caption.

name: b-over-the-nurse-shoulder
idea: Beat B, today, from just over the nurse's shoulder: her blurred scrub shoulder and tied-back hair at the bottom edge, and the rich man's face and top hat filling the middle of the frame, mid-dismissal, eyelids half shut, cigar in the corner of his mouth, palm up toward her. Pen and ink with cool blue-grey wash, early morning after a night shift, low pale sun behind him rimming his hat. Behind him, small and lightly drawn, a city of glass towers. Clear sky above his hat for the caption.

name: c-banknote-engraving-portrait
idea: Beat C, the reference frame. A frontal, chest-up portrait of the rich man alone, rendered like a steel engraving on old currency: fine parallel and curved hatching lines building every fold of jowl, waistcoat and hat, set inside a plain oval vignette on cream paper, no ornament words or numerals. He looks straight out with a small satisfied smile, one hand at his watch chain. Even, flat studio light so every feature reads clearly for reuse as the character reference. Large blank paper above and below the oval for the caption.

name: c-split-century-bench
idea: Beat C, one vertical frame cut in two by a torn-paper seam across the middle. Top half: the bench in 1919, drawn in sepia pen and ink, empty except for the rich man at one end. Bottom half: the same bench today in the same pen, but with bin, phone-lit commuter passing, and LED lamp post, and the same man at the same end in the identical pose, hat tilted at the same angle. Both halves share one consistent afternoon side-light from the left so the match is exact. The joke is that nothing about him changed; caption sits on the torn seam.

name: c-alone-at-sunset-wide
idea: Beat C, the button. A long, low, almost ground-level view along the path to the bench at sunset, the rich man alone in the exact centre, both sides of the bench empty, long ink shadow stretched toward the viewer. Brush and ink wash in warm sepia and grey, the sky a graded wash with nothing in it, leaving the top half free for the caption. Pigeons peck at his polished shoes; he looks relaxed, patient, waiting for the next person to sit down. The focus is on him; the foreground path softens.
